article_title: Surgeons' participation in the development of collaboration and management competencies in undergraduate medical education.
citation: Rothdiener M, Griewatz J, Meder A, Dall'Acqua A, Obertacke U, Kirschniak A, Borucki K, Koenig S, Ruesseler M, Steffens S, Steinweg B, Lammerding-Koeppel M. (2020). Surgeons' participation in the development of collaboration and management competencies in undergraduate medical education. PLoS ONE 15(6): e0233400. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0233400
title: NKLM professional roles Collaborator and Manager (based on CanMEDs) as a framework for competency-based surgical education
description: The NKLM (National Competency-based Learning Objectives for Undergraduate Medical Education) defines collaboration and management competencies in chapters 8 (Collaborator) and 10 (Manager), based on the CanMEDS framework. The Collaborator describes the work of physicians in an interprofessional health care team, whose central purpose is to prevent, negotiate and resolve interpersonal and interprofessional conflicts. The Manager role describes management and leadership competencies necessary in dealing with complex situations, including health economics, healthcare strategy, personnel and process management, and shared collaborative decision-making. Competency levels are defined at milestones, ranging from knowledge/understanding/basic skills to competency in practice, supervised and independent.
requirements: Professional roles are characterized by communication and interaction with different groups and by working in intersecting settings
constraints: For single objectives concerning economic aspects of the healthcare system and leadership development, the NKLM gives no standards for undergraduate education, recommending them only at postgraduate stage
examples: Mapping surgical courses at eight faculties against NKLM chapters 8 and 10 using the MERlin platform

article_title: Health information technology (IT) to improve the care of patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD).
citation: Diamantidis Clarissa J, Becker Stefan. (2014). Health information technology (IT) to improve the care of patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). BMC Nephrology. https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2369-15-7
title: NKDEP website: web-based kidney disease education for patients at elementary reading level
description: The National Kidney Disease Education Program (NKDEP) sponsors kidney disease education via digital media; its website contains links to educational topics targeted at patients rather than providers. Materials are available for download and print as educational supplements during provider-patient interactions that patients can take home. The review notes the content "is directed at an elementary school level reading capability, and has been modified based on an iterative process of review".
requirements: Content maintained at an elementary school reading level and revised through iterative review
examples: Downloadable and printable materials used as educational supplements during provider-patient interactions
key_sources: Diamantidis Clarissa J, Becker Stefan. (2014). Health information technology (IT) to improve the care of patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). BMC Nephrology. https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2369-15-7
